facts.raw_span: A man in his 60s presented with an enlarging purpuric patch on his left lateral superior forehead and left anterior scalp
initially present for 2 weeks
the lesion first developed in March 2014 and was fairly stable until June 2014
rapid growth and extension followed by central ulceration and bleeding
a 30 × 25-cm centrally eroded purpuric plaque with multifocal peripheral reddish-purple patches, papules, and macules
involving: Left anterior scalp with extension posteriorly on left parietal scalp
No evidence of lymphadenopathy in preauricular, cervical, occipital, submandibular or supraclavicular areas
Dermis permeated by irregular, slitlike spaces containing erythrocytes and lined by plump oval cells
Cells had pale eosinophilic cytoplasm and hyperchromatic nuclei
Cells stained positively with CD31 and were negative for CK5
No evidence of nodal, pulmonary, or liver metastases
Staging: T2N0M0

concepts.why: The presence of purpuric patches, rapid growth, and ulceration, along with the histopathological findings of irregular slitlike spaces containing erythrocytes and cells staining positively with CD31, are consistent with Kaposi's Sarcoma.

The rapid growth, ulceration, and presence of a large purpuric plaque, along with the histopathological findings of irregular slitlike spaces containing erythrocytes, are consistent with Angiosarcoma.

The presence of a purpuric patch with multifocal peripheral reddish-purple patches, papules, and macules, along with the histopathological findings of irregular slitlike spaces containing erythrocytes, are consistent with Hemangioma.
The presence of a purpuric patch with multifocal peripheral reddish-purple patches, papules, and macules, along with the absence of lymphadenopathy, are consistent with Pyogenic Granuloma.

The presence of a purpuric patch with multifocal peripheral reddish-purple patches, papules, and macules, along with the histopathological findings of irregular slitlike spaces containing erythrocytes, are consistent with Bacillary Angiomatosis.
The presence of a purpuric patch with multifocal peripheral reddish-purple patches, papules, and macules, along with the absence of lymphadenopathy, are consistent with Mycosis Fungoides.
The presence of rapid growth, ulceration, and the absence of nodal, pulmonary, or liver metastases, are consistent with Lymphoma.
The presence of a purpuric patch with multifocal peripheral reddish-purple patches, papules, and macules, along with the absence of lymphadenopathy, are consistent with Leukemia Cutis.
